doc_title: YouTube: How Real Apps Are Built: System Design for the AI Era | Episode 1
title: System Design for a Traditional Web Application
content: Handle real-world workload, and your application will still fail. Simplify a traditional web application by imagining an online shopping website. The first interaction is with the frontend, what you see. A request for a product is sent to the backend server, which may need information about the product, so it queries the database. The database returns the information, and eventually, the response comes back to you. At a basic level, we have a user, frontend, backend, and database. However, real systems quickly become more complicated. A cache might be added to return frequently requested information faster. Multiple servers may be used, and a load balancer could distribute users between them. Tools that don't need to happen immediately might be needed, and separate services for users, payments, products, and notifications could be implemented. Suddenly, a simple application becomes complex.
